fields.v: Infobip phased workflow for operating coding agents (extends the research-plan-implement paradigm of Horthy 2025). Version: Not stated. Materials: github.com/infobip/agentic-development-workflow

Curated research document (validated findings); persistent plan artifact (validated decisions, replaces the conversation); machine-readable tasks (stable identifier, goal, dependencies, relevant code paths, acceptance criteria, validation method); task registry (status, dependencies, acceptance criteria, latest outcome); append-only activity log (actions, validation results, changed files/commits, failures, next action); hand-crafted project-level instructions (concise single-line corrections); git for code state

Research -> planning (once per project) -> task definition -> implementation (repeated per task; return to task definition when a task is poorly defined instead of patching the code). In each phase four context strategies (write, select, compress, isolate) against four failure modes (distraction, confusion, poisoning, clash). Implementation: fresh session per task; implement, validate, log, update status, commit, terminate

Human effort front-loaded: research findings validated before proceeding; practitioner manually curates the plan to validated decisions; tasks defined with acceptance criteria; implementation under manual supervision or in an autonomous loop; practitioner reviews output rather than writing it; adds corrections to project instructions when the agent repeats mistakes
Not run (document-based description of practice; no study conducted)

Not classifiable (closest: spec-first). Authors' wording: 'phased workflow', 'research-plan-implement paradigm', 'user harness'; the plan and task artefacts persist across the project's phases and replace conversation state
